answer_1.quote: To address this dearth of realistic benchmarks for game dialogue authoring, we introduce KNUDGE: KNowledge constrained User-NPC Dialogue GEneration, a set of dialogue trees (in English) extracted from The Outer Worlds, an existing video game, and paired with granular ontological constraints. ... We pose the task of knowledge-constrained NPC dialogue generation ...

answer_2.quote: We measured human judgments of NPC desiderata and various automatic metrics ... We also evaluate overlap against the following single-and multi-reference sets: 1) the gold utterance n i , 2) the quest statements in Q, and 3) the biography statements in B. ... We use re-scaled BERTScore-F1 . as well as GPT-4-produced scores ...

answer_3.quote: Given the extensive overhead required for human evaluation of full dialogues, we used GPT-4 following recent work  that finds 'strong LLM judges like GPT-4 can match both controlled and crowdsourced human preferences well' . We verified GPT-4's correlation with a human expert on a set of dialogues, then used GPT-4 to compare the full end-to-end pipeline with ablated baseline variants on all test quests in KNUDGE.

answer_4.quote: We conduct human evaluation to examine models' qualitative NUP performance. 100 generations per model were judged on a 4-point Likert scale for four criteria: 1. Coherence: does the utterance follow naturally from the utterances in the history? 2. (Non-)Violation: does the utterance create contradictions with any of the sentences in the ontology? 3. Biography Usage: does the utterance make use of the biographies in B? 4. Quest Usage: does the utterance progress the dialogue according to the quest details in Q?
answer_4.guideline: Annotators judged on a 4-point Likert scale for four criteria with definitions provided: Coherence, (Non-)Violation, Biography Usage, Quest Usage.
